items.readable_text:
Content:
A polyhedron is a [MATH: 3]-dimensional shape where each side is a polygon. These flat polygonal sides are called faces.

Content:
Prisms are polyhedrons made of two identical polygonal faces (called bases) connected by equal parallel line segments. If these line segments are perpendicular to the bases, we have a right prism.

Content:
Let's take a look at some common prisms.

Content:
- A triangular (right) prism consists of two identical triangular faces connected by equal parallel line segments.

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/c8fbfb306c61e5d397e8c8db898213cd]

Content:
- A rectangular (right) prism consists of two identical rectangular faces connected by equal parallel line segments. Notice that each face is a rectangle.

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/1b3bbeaca26b7551afb93a8f41621a53]

Content:
- A cube is a special case of a rectangular prism that consists of six equal square faces.

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/5eeaa36f43863fbdcbd355fb766543e3]

Content:
By adding more sides to the polygonal base, we can make more prisms. For example, the following shape is a pentagonal prism.

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/cfd4d398f6c3a2b2c6b7469925b3be1f]

Content:
We can also construct hexagonal prisms, heptagonal prisms, etc.

lesson.readable_text:
Item 1 — Tutorial: Introduction

Content:
A polyhedron is a [MATH: 3]-dimensional shape where each side is a polygon. These flat polygonal sides are called faces.

Content:
Prisms are polyhedrons made of two identical polygonal faces (called bases) connected by equal parallel line segments. If these line segments are perpendicular to the bases, we have a right prism.

Content:
Let's take a look at some common prisms.

Content:
- A triangular (right) prism consists of two identical triangular faces connected by equal parallel line segments.

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/c8fbfb306c61e5d397e8c8db898213cd]

Content:
- A rectangular (right) prism consists of two identical rectangular faces connected by equal parallel line segments. Notice that each face is a rectangle.

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/1b3bbeaca26b7551afb93a8f41621a53]

Content:
- A cube is a special case of a rectangular prism that consists of six equal square faces.

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/5eeaa36f43863fbdcbd355fb766543e3]

Content:
By adding more sides to the polygonal base, we can make more prisms. For example, the following shape is a pentagonal prism.

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/cfd4d398f6c3a2b2c6b7469925b3be1f]

Content:
We can also construct hexagonal prisms, heptagonal prisms, etc.

---

Item 2 — Tutorial: Pyramids

Content:
Pyramids are polyhedrons made of a polygonal base, with the other triangular faces meeting at a single point.

Content:
Let's take a look at some common pyramids.

Content:
- A triangular pyramid has a triangular base with [MATH: 3] other triangular faces that meet at a single point.

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/bcbe0e4914077352e77072349fd4edf6]

Content:
- A rectangular pyramid has a rectangular base with [MATH: 4] triangular faces that meet at a single point. If the base is a square, we call this a square pyramid.

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/d3ac4e980627a17e6c160069d4f1901a]

Content:
- A pentagonal pyramid has a pentagonal base with [MATH: 5] triangular faces that meet at a single point.

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/a3fd2aa17b6bd452a0b37d76ee53af38]

Content:
Similarly to prisms, we can add more sides to the polygonal base to make more types of pyramids.

---

Content:
EXPLANATION

Explanation:
The polyhedron is a heptagonal prism since it has two identical heptagonal faces connected by equal parallel line segments.

Also, notice that:

- The solid is not an octagonal (pentagonal or hexagonal) prism since it does not have an octagonal (pentagonal or hexagonal) base.
- The solid is not a cube since not all of its faces are squares.
